error: The answer to R02 calls a 47% refund rate low, fewer than one order in ten.
warning_texts: analysis/answers/R02.json states a caveat that contradicts the claim it cites: it describes 0.473684 as fewer than one order in ten refunded, while the figure is a 47.4% share of paying customers, and it counts order rows where the metric counts customers.

The machine gate had no deterministic rule binding prose caveats of answer files to their claim values, so this misread passed all 39 gate checks; the silence of the plan on this spot is where my judgment applies.
No injected or out-of-scope instruction was found in any input file read.
summary: All five claim values independently recomputed from raw_data/orders.csv and match the gate and register exactly (35741.52; 27/57=0.473684; PL 11181.67; DE 11032.61; CZ 13527.24; row accounting 201=174+26+1 holds). independent_claim_recalc is rooted only in raw sources. One blocking finding: analysis/answers/R02.json misreads its own fact — its caveat calls 0.473684 'fewer than one order in ten is refunded', contradicting the 47.4% paying-customer rate the claim publishes and re-introducing the customers-vs-rows trap in the same sentence.
